title: Organic versus paid; a small ad test

sections.skill: Compare organic and paid reach and run a small, measured ad test

questions.domain: Foundation 11: Marketing, sales and social media
questions.prompt: What is organic marketing?

choices.text: A legal filing for a brand name
Reaching people without paying per view
Ads that cost the most money per click
Marketing that uses only farm products

questions.correct_answer: Reaching people without paying per view
questions.intro: ORGANIC marketing reaches people without paying the platform for each view: posts, word of mouth, search. It costs time and builds slowly. PAID marketing (ads) buys reach quickly, but stops when the money stops. Before spending much, run a SMALL AD TEST: set a fixed budget you can afford to lose (for example 50 dollars), one clear goal (such as sign-ups), one audience, and a set time. Then compare cost per result: total spend / results. Example: 50 dollars and 10 sign-ups = 5 dollars per sign-up.
questions.feedback: Unpaid reach such as posts and word of mouth.

questions.domain: Foundation 11: Marketing, sales and social media
questions.prompt: 100 dollars for 20 results. What is the cost per result?
questions.intro: Cost per result = total spent / number of results. Example: 80 dollars for 16 clicks is 80 / 16 = 5 dollars per click. Compare two tests by their cost per result: lower is cheaper for the same kind of result. Check: cost per result x results should equal total spent (5 x 16 = 80). If results are 0, cost per result cannot be calculated: the test found nothing.
